paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Xerxes has 127 provinces, a 180-day show-off party, gold goblets and gold couches, and one "no" from Queen Vashti is enough to send him up in flames (Esther 1:1-12). The text says he "became furious, and his anger burned within him" (Esther 1:12). All that power, and a man who can't handle one answer he didn't like.

Now look at what happens next. Instead of cooling off, he asks his advisors, and Memucan turns one refusal into a kingdom-wide crisis, with a decree that "cannot be repealed" (Esther 1:16-19). Angry people grab the biggest fix in reach and call it wisdom. I think that's worth a look in our own hearts, because we've all sent a reply or made a call while the oven was cranked to the top. Proverbs 15:1 says, "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger."

Here's what I want you to carry out of the kitchen. Human kings can write decrees in every language of the land (Esther 1:22), but a king's word is only as steady as his temper. This story isn't over, friend. Esther 1 sets the table, and the Bible has more to say about who is really in charge of this kingdom.
